findings.problem: The tag 'a real prime p: 617 digits' sits under '3231700607131100 ...', which are the leading digits of 2^2048 - 1 (A8.BIG). That number is not prime (it is divisible by 3: (2n**2048n - 1n) % 3n === 0n) and a real 2048-bit prime would not start with the digits of the largest 2048-bit number. The size claim (617 digits) is right; calling this number 'a real prime' is false, in a video whose rule is that every number is right.
findings.fix: Keep the caption 'A 617-digit prime makes that search hopeless' (true). Relabel the tag to 'p this size: 617 digits' (or 'a 2048-bit p: 617 digits') and rename the A8.BIG assertion so it no longer says prime; or replace the digits by 'p is about 3 x 10^616'.
findings.evidence: s4@13.2 to 14.8 (tag 'a real prime p: 617 digits'); scene-04-numbers.js line 240; node check of 2^2048 - 1 mod 3 = 0.

findings.problem: Eve's hunt ends with a green hit at x = 6 but her ghost 'a = ?' tag and 'x = ?' never resolve, so the hit has no consequence on screen. Lesson 8.3 (dhRun) says: with p this tiny she finds a = t in t tries, and only then that a 2048-bit prime makes the search impossible. As drawn a first-time learner can read '6 tries' as a failed or neutral search, and the contrast with the 617-digit case loses its point (the toy key IS broken).
findings.fix: When x = 6 turns green (12.6), turn the dashed purple 'a = ?' into a red solid 'a = 6' (D.a) with a small pop, so the toy secret visibly leaks; then the '617 digits' and 'no computer can search that' tags follow as now.
findings.evidence: s4@11.8 (a = ? still dashed), s4@13.2 and s4@14.6 (x = 6 green, 'a = ?' unchanged); lesson js/content/algo/algo-p8-x-02.js line 93.

findings.problem: Eve's red question mark beside her copy of XJHWJY says she cannot read this ciphertext, but it is a +5 shift cipher. Lesson 8.1 teaches the opposite for exactly this ciphertext: only 25 keys, caesarRun cracks XJHWJY in 5 tries, 'classical ciphers fall to brute force'. A learner who has just done 8.1 sees the video claim a 25-key cipher is unreadable.
findings.fix: Mark it as a stand-in: add a small grey tag 'toy shift cipher' near the +5 row (about 5.0 to 7.0 s), or extend caption 2 to 'A cipher scrambles it with a secret key (a toy shift here).' Keep the question mark only for 'without the key'.
findings.evidence: s2@6 (+5 tags, key 5), s2@7.9 (red XJHWJY copy with red ?); lesson algo-p8-x-01.js caesarRun (KEY 5, CT XJHWJY).

findings.problem: Caption 'Change one letter and every digit changes.' states as a rule what is only true of this example. For a good hash each hex digit stays the same with probability 1/16, so about 40% of one-letter edits leave at least one of 8 digits unchanged ((15/16)^8 = 0.60 for all 8 to differ). Lesson 8.5 says 'a totally different digest' and the avalanche check says about half the bits flip (18 of 32 for cat/cot), not every digit.
findings.fix: Caption: 'Change one letter and the whole fingerprint changes.' Keep the orange tag 'all 8 digits differ' (true for cat and cot), perhaps as 'here all 8 digits differ'.
findings.evidence: s7@7.3 and s7@9.5 (caption and tag); node: toy('cat') vs toy('cot') differ in 8 of 8 hex digits, 18 of 32 bits.

findings.problem: The headline 'Edit one block and every link after breaks' is contradicted by the picture and the lesson. After the edit only link 1-2 breaks; link 2-3 stays green with a tick until the forger patches block 2 (8.35 s). Lesson 8.5's own runner asks 'which block now has a broken link?' with answer block 2 only ('Block 3 only references block 2, whose content is unchanged'). The headline is on screen for the whole scene, including 5.5 to 8.3 s when link 2-3 is plainly valid.
findings.fix: Retitle to something the figure proves, for example ['Edit one block and', 'the break travels on'] (it breaks one link, and each repair moves the break one block along).
findings.evidence: s8@6.5 (link 1-2 red cross, link 2-3 green tick, headline says every link); lesson algo-p8-x-02.js chainRun ask at 'Block 2'.

findings.problem: Caption 4 (8.2 to 10.8) 'Recompute every later hash and it looks valid again.' claims the outcome while the picture still shows 'broken chain' (link 2-3 red from 8.35). The chain only looks valid again at 10.5 (last tick) and the 'valid chain' badge pops at 10.75, the caption's last 0.05 s. The outcome is never on screen while its caption is.
findings.fix: Caption 4 [8.2, 10.4]: 'Recompute each later hash to repair every link.'; let the 'valid chain' badge (10.75) and the existing caption 5 [11.0, 12.4] carry the outcome, or add [10.6, 12.4] 'It looks valid again. Hashes spot edits, they do not stop them.'
findings.evidence: s8@8.8 (caption says valid again; badge 'broken chain', link 2-3 red cross); s8@12.3 (valid chain).

findings.problem: Caption 5 (8.8 to 11.0) 'Each extra zero makes a hit 16 times rarer.' runs ahead of its picture. From 8.8 to about 10.2 only the 16-square strip and 'starts with 0: 1 in 16' are on screen; the second zero ('starts with 00: 1 in 256') pops at 10.6 and is fully in at 10.95, so the claim has evidence for 0.4 s of its 2.2 s window.
findings.fix: Re-time to the picture: [8.8, 10.5, 'One hash in 16 starts with 0.'], then [10.7, 12.2, 'Two zeros: one in 256.'], then [12.3, 13.3, 'So 16 times more work.'] (and move the 'work' sticker to about 12.2); or start caption 5 at 10.2.
findings.evidence: s9@9.3 (strip only, caption already says 16 times rarer), s9@10.3 (square half built), s9@10.9 (1 in 256 tag just in).

findings.problem: The scene's conclusion ('Rewriting history means redoing all that work', total '50 tries') has no scale. 50 hashes is trivial, the bars (15, 5, 30) vary by luck (block 2 took 5, block 3 took 30 under the same rule) and nothing links them to real difficulty, so a first-time learner can read forging as cheap. Lesson 8.7 prices the work (16 times per zero, trillions of hashes for a real block) and also says the rewrite must outrun the honest chain; neither appears. Scene 9's 16-times-per-zero rule is not connected to these bars.
findings.fix: Add a grey tag under the '50 tries' sticker at about 9.2 s: 'real blocks: trillions of tries each' (lesson 8.7 step 2, 'trillions of hashes'), and optionally 'about 16 tries per block here, on average'. Optionally end caption 5 with ', while the real chain keeps growing' only if it fits.
findings.evidence: s10@10.9 (bars 15, 5, 30 and '50 tries', no baseline); lesson algo-p8-x-04.js step 'Proof of work' and 'Rewriting history needs most of the power'.

findings.problem: Recap row 3 shows blocks 2 and 3 (and both links) turning red together right after the edit (red at 1.6 and 1.75 s of the pictogram, set in the storyboard too). In scenes 8 and 10 and in lesson 8.5 only link 1-2 breaks at the edit; link 2-3 breaks only after block 2 is repaired and re-sealed. The recap therefore re-teaches the headline's over-simplification and disagrees with the lesson's own quick check ('which block now has a broken link? block 2').
findings.fix: Order the pictogram as the real cascade: block 1 orange, block 2 red; block 1 green; block 2 re-sealed (green) and only then block 3 red (about 2.5 s); block 3 re-sealed at 2.9 s. Update the storyboard note 'blocks 2 and 3 turn red' to match.
findings.evidence: s11@5.5 (block 1 green, blocks 2 and 3 and both arrows red at once); scene-11-recap.js chainRow T.red = [1.6, 1.75].

findings.problem: The fingerprints (8 hex digits) come from the lesson's toy 32-bit hash but nothing on screen says so. Lesson 8.5 says 'This demo uses a toy 32-bit hash. Real systems use SHA-256.' A learner may think real hashes are 8 digits, and later scenes use the same toy digests as if they were real ('hash starts with 0' in hex, 8 digits).
findings.fix: Add a small grey tag under the middle machine, for example 'toy hash: 8 digits (real ones: 64)', or label the machine 'toy hash'.
findings.evidence: s7@9.5 (no 'toy' anywhere); grep of scene sources finds no on-screen 'toy', 'SHA' or 'bits'.

findings.problem: Block 1's 'prev ecaf011a' is the hash of an unseen block 0 (the lesson's genesis block, 'genesis' in chainRun) and is never labelled, so the learner meets an unexplained fingerprint at the start of the chain; scene 10 repeats it.
findings.fix: Add a tiny grey tag 'start of chain' near block 1's prev row at 0.2 to 1.4 s, or draw a short stub link into block 1 labelled 'start'.
findings.evidence: s8@4.7 and s10@3.2 (block 1: prev ecaf011a, no source); A8.CHAIN.genesis = toy('0|genesis|00000000').

findings.problem: From about 4.4 to 5.45 s the screen contradicts itself: block 1 already shows its new hash 9a1f8189 and block 2 still stores fb28ccb9, yet the check strip reads 'hash of block 1 = fb28ccb9' with a green tick, link 1-2 has a green tick and the badge says 'valid chain'. The strip only refreshes at 5.0 to 5.45.
findings.fix: Start the strip's refresh as soon as the hash roll ends (about 4.45), or dim the strip digits and badge to neutral while block 1's hash is changing (3.9 to 5.0).
findings.evidence: s8@4.7 (9a1f8189 in block 1, fb28ccb9 in the strip, 'valid chain').

findings.problem: Eve divides 55 by 2, 3, 4 and 5 ('four tries'). Dividing by 4 after 2 failed is pointless, and lesson 8.2 says trial division goes 'one prime at a time' (2, 3, 5, 7 ...). It matches lesson 8.4's Attack button (2, 3, 4, ...), so video and lesson 8.4 agree but the lessons disagree with each other. Also the conclusion jumps from '55 = 5 x 11' to 'so d = 27' without z = 40, which lesson 8.4 puts in between.
findings.fix: Either keep it (matches the interactive Attack) and reconcile lesson 8.2 when next edited, or use 2, 3, 5 and say 'three tries'. If it fits the row, make the tag 'so z = 40, d = 27'.

findings.problem: 'A real n has 617 digits' (caption and tag 'a real n: 617 digits') states one size. Lesson 8.3 and 8.4 say a real n has 2048+ bits; 617 digits is exactly the 2048-bit case, so larger real keys are longer.
findings.fix: Caption and tag: 'A real n has 617+ digits' (or 'a real n: 2048+ bits, 617+ digits' on the tag).
findings.evidence: s6@11.8; lesson algo-p8.js ('Real n has 2048+ bits').

findings.problem: 'Blockchain' appears only on the title card. Scenes 8 to 10 draw a hash chain and proof of work but never say that this is a blockchain or what Bitcoin miners do, so the title's second word is never connected to the content (the Bitcoin lesson 8.6 is also omitted, as the outline says).
findings.fix: Name it once, for example scene 8 caption 1: 'Each block stores the hash of the block before it: a blockchain.', or add 'Bitcoin miners do this' to scene 9's target tag.
findings.evidence: grep of scenes 2 to 11: no on-screen 'blockchain' or 'Bitcoin'; s1@3 title card.
